definition: Reciprocal Human Machine Learning (RHML) is an interdisciplinary approach to designing human-AI interaction systems.
details: RHML aims to enable continual learning between humans and machine learning models by having them learn from each other. This approach keeps the human expert "in the loop" to oversee and enhance machine learning performance and simultaneously support the human expert continue learning.

explainer.lead: Reciprocal Human Machine Learning is an interdisciplinary approach to designing human-AI interaction systems. It matters because it treats learning as two-way: the model improves and so does the human expert.

tiers.eli5: Like a chess coach and student who each get better because they keep playing and explaining to each other.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers keep the human expert in the loop to oversee and enhance model performance while the expert keeps learning from the system. A pitfall is designing the loop so the human only corrects the model, which drops the reciprocal half of the idea.
tiers.paperLevel: An interdisciplinary approach to human-AI interaction design aimed at continual learning between humans and models, with the human expert in the loop overseeing and enhancing machine learning performance while continuing to learn.

explainer.example: An expert reviews and corrects model predictions over time, and the corrections also sharpen the expert's own judgments.
